releaseNote.summary: Selection rules can read the caller's resolved roles via context.Caller; a role-provider outage fails a role-reading selection with 503 Authorization:110006.

scriptCallerRoles.description: ScriptContext.Caller (ICallerAccessor: HasRoleAsync, RolesAsync, IsAvailable, ResolutionFailed, RolesFromHeader) exposes the caller's role set as resolved by the configured caller-role provider (default: token claims, else the gateway role header; morph-idm: the identity service, a non-blank role header replaces its answer). Available only to rule-based selection on a caller's request: transition schemas (write validation and functions/schema), function inputSchema/outputSchema/inputView/outputView rules, state/transition views rules. Elsewhere (tasks, lifecycle tasks, automatic rules, timers, event handlers, Execution host) IsAvailable is false and a read throws CallerRolesUnavailableException; on function execute the accessor is closed after input-schema selection, before the cache key and tasks. Resolved lazily on the first read, at most once per request (shared with the provider's per-request memo); rules that never read roles cost no provider call. If a rule reads roles and the provider fails, the selection fails with 503 Authorization:110006 (retryable) whatever the rule returned or swallowed, and nothing is cached; rules that do not read roles are unaffected. Role selection is UX/contract selection, not authorization. PURELY ADDITIVE.
